questions.question: How do you write a robust font-family stack?
questions.answer: List preferred fonts first and end with a generic family, quoting multi-word names: Inter, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif. This guarantees a usable fallback if a font is missing.

questions.question: Why is a unitless line-height preferred?
questions.answer: A unitless value multiplies each element's own font size, so children scale correctly. Fixed px or em line-heights can inherit a value that is too tight or too loose for the child's font size.

questions.question: What does font-display: swap do?
questions.answer: It shows fallback text immediately and swaps to the custom font when it loads, avoiding invisible text but causing a visible font swap. block delays text, fallback uses a short block, optional uses the font only if fast.

questions.question: What is the difference between text-transform and changing the actual text?
questions.answer: text-transform changes visual casing only; the DOM text and accessible name keep their original casing. Screen readers and copy-paste use the underlying text, so don't rely on it for meaningful changes.

questions.question: How do you truncate a single line with an ellipsis?
questions.answer: Set white-space: nowrap, overflow: hidden, and text-overflow: ellipsis on a width-constrained element. All three are required; without nowrap the text wraps instead.

questions.question: Create a fluid heading with balanced wrapping and a 1.15 line-height.
Why does font: 600 1.25rem Inter reset other font properties?
questions.answer: The font shorthand sets all font longhands (style, variant, weight, size, line-height, family) and resets omitted ones to initial. Declare longhands after the shorthand if you need overrides.

questions.question: Why can a px line-height look broken inside a larger heading?
questions.answer: A fixed line-height does not scale with font size, so it can be too tight for large type or too loose for small type. Use a unitless multiplier so each element computes leading from its own size.
